question: In which year was the name 'Pakistan' coined?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1933**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The name 'Pakistan' was coined by **Choudhry Rahmat Ali** in 1933.
 
• He was a prominent figure in the Pakistan Movement, which sought to create a separate Muslim state.
 
• The term 'Pakistan' is an acronym composed of letters taken from the names of the five northern regions of the British India: **Punjab, Afghania (North-West Frontier Province), Kashmir, Sindh, and Baluchistan**.
 
• The name also means 'Land of the Pure' in Urdu and Persian, reflecting the desire for a state that would uphold Islamic values.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pakistan Movement**

 
 
• The Pakistan Movement was a political movement in the 1940s that aimed for the creation of Pakistan, a separate nation for Muslims, from the regions of British India.
 
• The movement was led by the All-India Muslim League under the leadership of Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
 
• The demand for Pakistan was formalized on March 23, 1940, through the Lahore Resolution.
 
• The movement culminated in the creation of Pakistan on August 14, 1947, following the partition of India.
 
 
 
• **Choudhry Rahmat Ali**
 
 
• Choudhry Rahmat Ali was an Indian Muslim nationalist who is credited with creating the name 'Pakistan' for the separate Muslim state.
 
• He was born in 1897 in the Punjab Province of British India.
 
• He published a pamphlet titled "Now or Never" in 1933, in which he articulated his vision for a separate Muslim state and proposed the name 'Pakistan'.
 
• Rahmat Ali's vision played a significant role in shaping the aspirations of Muslims in British India and the eventual creation of Pakistan.
